rust_locations: crates/rustuml-parser/src/preprocess/mod.rs#Value::to_display: Value::Utf16 projects through String::from_utf16_lossy, so the unit becomes U+FFFD and a normal diagram exits 0.
crates/rustuml-parser/src/preprocess/mod.rs#substitute_vars and the standalone-call return path: the two places a TIM value becomes diagram line text.
crates/rustuml-parser/src/parse/mod.rs#parse_with_base: where a TIM fatal error becomes ParseError and a nonzero CLI exit.
causal_divergence: Rust String cannot hold a lone surrogate. The UTF-16 port keeps it in memory, but the lossy projection hides the failure that Java hits at export, so a Java crash diagram becomes a Rust normal diagram (a lost rejection).
invariant: When TIM projects a value holding an unpaired surrogate into a diagram content line, and parsing otherwise succeeds, the Rust outcome is a structured error with a nonzero CLI exit carrying Java's SAX message for the first such unit. A TIM fatal error or a parser error anywhere in the block takes precedence, as in Java, where those stop before export. Values that never become content-line text (assignments, conditions, unused variables) stay legal.
planned_change: Record the first unpaired unit seen when substitute_vars or the standalone-call return path projects a value into a content line (PreprocessOutput.export_failure, separate from the fatal TIM error). parse_with_base returns it as ParseError after a successful family parse. No crash SVG is produced and no character is deleted.
declared_residue: Java fails only if the text reaches the SVG writer. A content line that the parser discards (a ' comment, a hidden entity's label, an unused skinparam value) still triggers the Rust error, where Java may render normally. The probes include one such line so the residue is measured, not assumed.
The Java message distinguishes 'character data content' from 'attribute value'; Rust reports the character data form for every unit.
